after.name: Question 1
after.problem: What is ${\int }_{e}^{3e}ln⁡x\,\text{d}x$ expressed as the limit of a left Riemann sum?
after.worked_solution:
The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a left Riemann sum as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx,
$$

    

where $Δx=\frac{b-a}{n}$ and ${x}_{i}=a+iΔx.$

In the definite integral

$$
{\int }_{e}^{3e}ln⁡x\,\text{d}x,
$$

the function is $f(x)=ln⁡x,$ the lower bound is $a=e,$ and the upper bound is $b=3e.$ So, we have

$$
Δx=\frac{3e-e}{n}=\frac{2e}{n},
$$

and therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{e}^{3e}ln⁡x\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[f(e+i\cdot \frac{2e}{n})\cdot \frac{2e}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[f(e+\frac{2ie}{n})\cdot \frac{2e}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[ln⁡(e+\frac{2ie}{n})\cdot \frac{2e}{n}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem: What is ${\int }_{e}^{3e}ln⁡x\,\text{d}x$ expressed as the limit of a left Riemann sum?
content.worked_solution:
The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a left Riemann sum as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx,
$$

    

where $Δx=\frac{b-a}{n}$ and ${x}_{i}=a+iΔx.$

In the definite integral

$$
{\int }_{e}^{3e}ln⁡x\,\text{d}x,
$$

the function is $f(x)=ln⁡x,$ the lower bound is $a=e,$ and the upper bound is $b=3e.$ So, we have

$$
Δx=\frac{3e-e}{n}=\frac{2e}{n},
$$

and therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{e}^{3e}ln⁡x\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[f(e+i\cdot \frac{2e}{n})\cdot \frac{2e}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[f(e+\frac{2ie}{n})\cdot \frac{2e}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[ln⁡(e+\frac{2ie}{n})\cdot \frac{2e}{n}].\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: The width is Δx=(-2−(-4))/n=2/n, and the left endpoints are x_j=-4+2j/n for j=0,…,n−1. Substituting into -5x^(-2) and multiplying by Δx gives option d.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: What is ${\int }_{-4}^{-2}-5{x}^{-2}\,\text{d}x$ expressed as the limit of a left Riemann sum?
after.worked_solution:
The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a left Riemann sum as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{j=0}^{n-1}f({x}_{j})\cdot Δx,
$$

    

where $Δx=\frac{b-a}{n}$ and ${x}_{j}=a+jΔx.$

In the definite integral

$$
{\int }_{-4}^{-2}-5{x}^{-2}\,\text{d}x,
$$

the function is $f(x)=-5{x}^{-2},$ the lower bound is $a=-4,$ and the upper bound is $b=-2.$ So, we have

$$
Δx=\frac{-2-(-4)}{n}=\frac{2}{n},
$$

and therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{-2}-5{x}^{-2}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{j=0}^{n-1}f({x}_{j})\cdot Δx \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{j=0}^{n-1}[f(-4+j\cdot \frac{2}{n})\cdot \frac{2}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{j=0}^{n-1}[f(-4+\frac{2j}{n})\cdot \frac{2}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{j=0}^{n-1}[-5{(-4+\frac{2j}{n})}^{-2}\cdot \frac{2}{n}].\end{aligned}
$$

Correct
EXPLANATION

The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a left Riemann sum as

∫abf(x)dx=limn→∞∑j=0n−1f(xj)⋅Δx,

where Δx=b−an and xj=a+jΔx.

In the definite integral

∫−4−2−5x−2dx,

the function is f(x)=−5x−2, the lower bound is a=−4, and the upper bound is b=−2. So, we have

Δx=−2−(−4)n=2n,

and therefore

∫−4−2−5x−2dx=limn→∞∑j=0n−1f(xj)⋅Δx=limn→∞∑j=0n−1[f(−4+j⋅2n)⋅2n]=limn→∞∑j=0n−1[f(−4+2jn)⋅2n]=limn→∞∑j=0n−1[−5(−4+2jn)−2⋅2n].

content.problem: What is ${\int }_{-4}^{-2}-5{x}^{-2}\,\text{d}x$ expressed as the limit of a left Riemann sum?
content.worked_solution:
The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a left Riemann sum as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{j=0}^{n-1}f({x}_{j})\cdot Δx,
$$

    

where $Δx=\frac{b-a}{n}$ and ${x}_{j}=a+jΔx.$

In the definite integral

$$
{\int }_{-4}^{-2}-5{x}^{-2}\,\text{d}x,
$$

the function is $f(x)=-5{x}^{-2},$ the lower bound is $a=-4,$ and the upper bound is $b=-2.$ So, we have

$$
Δx=\frac{-2-(-4)}{n}=\frac{2}{n},
$$

and therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{-2}-5{x}^{-2}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{j=0}^{n-1}f({x}_{j})\cdot Δx \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{j=0}^{n-1}[f(-4+j\cdot \frac{2}{n})\cdot \frac{2}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{j=0}^{n-1}[f(-4+\frac{2j}{n})\cdot \frac{2}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{j=0}^{n-1}[-5{(-4+\frac{2j}{n})}^{-2}\cdot \frac{2}{n}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 3
after.problem: What is ${\int }_{-2}^{3}-2{x}^{3}\text{d}x$ expressed as the limit of a right Riemann sum?
after.worked_solution:
The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a right Riemann sum as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{k=1}^{n}f({x}_{k})\cdot Δx,
$$

where ${x}_{k}=a+kΔx$ and $Δx=\frac{b-a}{n}.$

In the definite integral

$$
{\int }_{-2}^{3}-2{x}^{3}\text{d}x,
$$

the function is $f(x)=-2{x}^{3},$ the lower bound is $a=-2$ and the upper bound is $b=3.$ So, we have

$$
Δx=\frac{3-(-2)}{n}=\frac{5}{n}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{3}-2{x}^{3}\text{d}x & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{k=1}^{n}f({x}_{k})\cdot Δx \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{k=1}^{n}[f(-2+k\cdot \frac{5}{n})\cdot \frac{5}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{k=1}^{n}[f(-2+\frac{5k}{n})\cdot \frac{5}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{k=1}^{n}[-2{(-2+\frac{5k}{n})}^{3}\cdot \frac{5}{n}].\end{aligned}
$$

Submit

EXPLANATION

The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a right Riemann sum as

∫abf(x)dx=limn→∞∑k=1nf(xk)⋅Δx,

where xk=a+kΔx and Δx=b−an.

In the definite integral

∫−23−2x3dx,

the function is f(x)=−2x3, the lower bound is a=−2 and the upper bound is b=3. So, we have

Δx=3−(−2)n=5n.

Therefore,

∫−23−2x3dx=limn→∞∑k=1nf(xk)⋅Δx=limn→∞∑k=1n[f(−2+k⋅5n)⋅5n]=limn→∞∑k=1n[f(−2+5kn)⋅5n]=limn→∞∑k=1n[−2(−2+5kn)3⋅5n].

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms c. The interval width is Δx=5/n, and the right endpoints are x_k=−2+5k/n for k=1,…,n. Thus each summand is −2(−2+5k/n)³·5/n.

content.problem: What is ${\int }_{-2}^{3}-2{x}^{3}\text{d}x$ expressed as the limit of a right Riemann sum?
content.worked_solution:
The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a right Riemann sum as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{k=1}^{n}f({x}_{k})\cdot Δx,
$$

where ${x}_{k}=a+kΔx$ and $Δx=\frac{b-a}{n}.$

In the definite integral

$$
{\int }_{-2}^{3}-2{x}^{3}\text{d}x,
$$

the function is $f(x)=-2{x}^{3},$ the lower bound is $a=-2$ and the upper bound is $b=3.$ So, we have

$$
Δx=\frac{3-(-2)}{n}=\frac{5}{n}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{3}-2{x}^{3}\text{d}x & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{k=1}^{n}f({x}_{k})\cdot Δx \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{k=1}^{n}[f(-2+k\cdot \frac{5}{n})\cdot \frac{5}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{k=1}^{n}[f(-2+\frac{5k}{n})\cdot \frac{5}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{k=1}^{n}[-2{(-2+\frac{5k}{n})}^{3}\cdot \frac{5}{n}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: What is ${\int }_{1}^{6}ln⁡(4x-3)\,\text{d}x$ expressed as the limit of a right Riemann sum?
after.worked_solution:
The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a right Riemann sum as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{m=1}^{n}f({x}_{m})\cdot Δx,
$$

where ${x}_{m}=a+mΔx$ and $Δx=\frac{b-a}{n}.$

In the definite integral

$$
{\int }_{1}^{6}ln⁡(4x-3)\,\text{d}x,
$$

the function is $f(x)=ln⁡(4x-3),$ the lower bound is $a=1$ and the upper bound is $b=6.$ So, we have

$$
Δx=\frac{6-1}{n}=\frac{5}{n}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{6}ln⁡(4x-3)\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{m=1}^{n}f({x}_{m})\cdot Δx \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{m=1}^{n}[f(1+m\cdot \frac{5}{n})\cdot \frac{5}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{m=1}^{n}[f(1+\frac{5m}{n})\cdot \frac{5}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{m=1}^{n}[ln⁡(4(1+\frac{5m}{n})-3)\cdot \frac{5}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{m=1}^{n}[ln⁡(1+\frac{20m}{n})\cdot \frac{5}{n}].\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a right Riemann sum as

∫abf(x)dx=limn→∞∑m=1nf(xm)⋅Δx,

where xm=a+mΔx and Δx=b−an.

In the definite integral

∫16ln⁡(4x−3)dx,

the function is f(x)=ln⁡(4x−3), the lower bound is a=1 and the upper bound is b=6. So, we have

Δx=6−1n=5n.

Therefore, ∫16ln⁡(4x−3)dx=limn→∞∑m=1nf(xm)⋅Δx=limn→∞∑m=1n[f(1+m⋅5n)⋅5n]=limn→∞∑m=1n[f(1+5mn)⋅5n]=limn→∞∑m=1n[ln⁡(4(1+5mn)−3)⋅5n]=limn→∞∑m=1n[ln⁡(1+20mn)⋅5n].

content.problem: What is ${\int }_{1}^{6}ln⁡(4x-3)\,\text{d}x$ expressed as the limit of a right Riemann sum?
content.worked_solution:
The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a right Riemann sum as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{m=1}^{n}f({x}_{m})\cdot Δx,
$$

where ${x}_{m}=a+mΔx$ and $Δx=\frac{b-a}{n}.$

In the definite integral

$$
{\int }_{1}^{6}ln⁡(4x-3)\,\text{d}x,
$$

the function is $f(x)=ln⁡(4x-3),$ the lower bound is $a=1$ and the upper bound is $b=6.$ So, we have

$$
Δx=\frac{6-1}{n}=\frac{5}{n}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{6}ln⁡(4x-3)\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{m=1}^{n}f({x}_{m})\cdot Δx \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{m=1}^{n}[f(1+m\cdot \frac{5}{n})\cdot \frac{5}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{m=1}^{n}[f(1+\frac{5m}{n})\cdot \frac{5}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{m=1}^{n}[ln⁡(4(1+\frac{5m}{n})-3)\cdot \frac{5}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{m=1}^{n}[ln⁡(1+\frac{20m}{n})\cdot \frac{5}{n}].\end{aligned}
$$
